content:
The Kennedy Center board plans to propose adding President Trump's name to the building's facade to recognise him for rescuing it from a "precarious financial situation," according to new court documents in a lawsuit aimed at preventing such action.

This is the latest development in a case over adding the president's name to the cultural facility on the Potomac River in Washington, and reflects efforts by the Trump-aligned board to honour the president.

The new information comes from filings to the court by Democratic Representative Joyce Beatty of Ohio, an ex-officio member of the board. Beatty has led the effort to block Trump from adding his name to the building, and said in her filing that she was informing the court of the proposal because it could implicate a pending court decision.

The court and the Kennedy Center board are each scheduled to meet on Tuesday.

Beatty's filing includes two exhibits. The first is a draft vote to close the centre, claiming the building was unfit for use. According to Beatty, the statement misrepresented the findings of a consulting firm that "explicitly stated it provided no such opinion."

The other document claims the centre faces a severe financial situation. It explicitly calls for Trump's name to be carved in marble below the centre's name on the building's exterior. It offers ten possible inscriptions, including one that reads: "Renovations and donations overseen by President Donald J. Trump and the Trump Kennedy Center Fund." Another proposes: "With gratitude to President Donald J. Trump and the Trump Kennedy Center Fund."

In the proposed resolution, the board wrote: "The Board understands that without such appropriate recognition, President Trump would be less likely to provide the necessary oversight for the renovation of the main building or to lead the centre's financial rescue."

Trump has dramatically reshaped Washington in his second term, including tearing down the White House's East Wing to build a ballroom, planning an arch near Arlington National Cemetery and a revamped golf course along the Potomac.

The Kennedy Center has been a sticking point in those reshaping efforts, after a judge ruled in May that Trump's name was added unlawfully and ordered it removed.

But Trump and his allies have continued to fight the ruling.

The board voted last month to engrave his name on the building's exterior in full: "The John F. Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts, restored and renovated by President Donald J. Trump."

If the Trump Kennedy Center Fund raises $100 million, a second inscription will be added, reading: "Gift of the Trump Kennedy Center Fund."
